title: Know what you already own: the one-hour home inventory
description: Most homes contain duplicates bought in ignorance: the third bottle of the same spice, the cable that was already in a drawer. One hour with a notebook, room by room, stops you buying your own belongings back.
author: SparkKindly · AI-assisted

body.heading: Walk the rooms with a notebook
paragraphs: Take a notebook and walk your home slowly, listing what you own in the categories you actually buy: cleaning supplies, toiletries, cables and chargers, batteries, tools, stationery, pantry staples. You are not cataloguing every object — only the repeat-purchase zones where duplicates hide.
Open the backs of cupboards and the bottoms of drawers. Duplicates live at the back, behind the thing you bought to replace them.

body.heading: What the list changes
paragraphs: Shop from the list before you shop from the store. Half of “we need…” evaporates when a note on the fridge door says there are already two. The list also ends the emergency purchase — the full-price replacement bought in a panic for something sitting at home in a drawer.
Photograph the pages and keep them on your phone. An inventory you cannot check in the shop aisle is a diary, not a tool.

body.heading: Keep it alive in five minutes a month
paragraphs: Cross things off as they run out, and add a line when something new arrives. Five minutes a month keeps the list true, and a true list quietly pays for itself every single week.
There is a side effect people report with surprise: gratitude. A home you have actually counted looks less like a place that needs more, and more like a place that already has plenty.

takeaway: List the repeat-purchase zones of your home once, shop from the list, and stop buying duplicates of things you already own.
